text: Wrap search term (several) `contains()` passing exact-match argument [get_society()] [dp_societies()] – `soc_id`, `glottocode`, `iso_code`, `region`, `contribution_id`, `language_level_glottocodes` – match values merely contain term (via [grepl()]) instead requiring exact match. turns `get_society(region = "Africa")` (matches nothing, since D-PLACE region literally called `"Africa"` – see `unique(dplace_societies$region)`) `get_society(region = contains("Africa"))` (matches every region whose name contains "Africa").

title: Browse or filter D-PLACE societies — dp_societies
text: glottocode Optional character vector Glottocodes filter , [contains()] partial/regex match. region Optional character vector regions filter (matched exactly `region` column; see `unique(dplace_societies$region)` valid values), [contains()] partial/regex match – e.g. `region = contains("Africa")`, since D-PLACE splits Africa several regions single `"Africa"` value. soc_id Optional character vector society IDs filter , [contains()] partial/regex match. Also accepts data frame/tibble `soc_id` column (e.g. earlier `dp_societies()` result passed straight ), column used automatically. xd_id Optional character vector cross-dataset ID(s) filter , [contains()] partial/regex match – see [get_related_societies()] finding society's `xd_id` first place. societies `xd_id` (`NA`) never match. lang_family Optional character vector top-level language family name(s) filter (e.g. `"Indo-European"`, `"Austronesian"`), [contains()] partial/regex match – see [dp_lang_family_list()] full list available families. isolate (e.g. `"Zuni"`) top-level family. Named `lang_family` (plain `family`) avoid clashing D-PLACE's "family" cultural/kinship variables, mean something unrelated. lang_family_id Optional character vector top-level language family Glottocode(s) filter (e.g. `"indo1319"` Indo-European), [contains()] partial/regex match – stable `lang_family` across future family renaming. type Character; row types include. Defaults `"society"` (societies coded cultural data). Use `NULL` also include `"languoid"` rows (language varieties appear phylogeny, coded data ). support [contains()].

title: dplaceR 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Bundles snapshot D-PLACE CLDF dataset (v3.3.0). Functions browse societies (dp_societies()), variables (dp_variables(), dp_search_variables()), codes (dp_codes()), values (dp_values(), dp_variable_data()), dataset contributions (dp_contributions()), language phylogenies (dp_trees(), dp_tree()). dp_citation() prints citation licence information bundled data. get_pairwise_geo_distance() computes pairwise least-cost, land-route geographic distances societies using ‘geoGraph’ package (Andrea Manica’s group; CRAN, installed separately – see function’s documentation). get_pairwise_cult_distance() computes pairwise cultural (dis)similarity societies one coded D-PLACE variables, configurable handling missing data (missing), returned metric (metric), optional type-aware scoring ordinal/continuous variables (type_aware). get_geo_distance() computes geographic (land-route) distance single point – D-PLACE society arbitrary coordinate – list societies, using method get_pairwise_geo_distance(). get_cult_distance() computes cultural distance single reference culture – D-PLACE society, custom profile, computed modal (common) profile across group societies – list societies, using method get_pairwise_cult_distance(). get_society_meta() appends society metadata (name, region, coordinates, etc.) tibble society ID, auto-detecting soc_id/soc_id_1/ soc_id_2 columns produced package’s functions. dp_map_societies() plots societies world map (via ‘ggplot2’ ‘maps’), optionally coloured another column labelled society ID. get_society_country() reverse-geocodes society’s coordinates country name (via ‘maps’), since D-PLACE records broad, multi-country world region – country. get_society() searches societies matching metadata criteria: exact-match filters soc_id, glottocode, iso_code, region, type, contribution_id, language_level_glottocodes; case-insensitive partial match name; single-value--range matching latitude, longitude, main_focal_year; country filter (via get_society_country() ‘maps’ package) applied last, every criterion narrowed search. supplied criteria combine . contains() switches exact-match argument get_society()/ dp_societies() (soc_id, glottocode, iso_code, region, contribution_id, language_level_glottocodes) partial/regex match via grepl() instead – e.g. get_society(region = contains("Africa")), since D-PLACE splits Africa several regions (“Southern Africa”, “West Tropical Africa”, etc.) single region literally called "Africa". Supports multiple patterns (matched ), ignore.case (default TRUE), fixed (literal instead regex). supported type, name (already partial match), country (already case-insensitive), numeric arguments. get_pairwise_language_distance() get_language_distance() compute linguistic (branch-length/“patristic”) distance societies’ languages bundled D-PLACE language tree (dp_trees()/dp_tree()), mirroring get_pairwise_geo_distance()/get_geo_distance()‘s pairwise/single-point split. Societies matched tree tips via glottocode, falling back language_level_glottocodes names single Glottocode; get_language_distance()’s point can D-PLACE society ID bare Glottocode. Two important caveats: branch length units consistent across D-PLACE’s 114 bundled trees – Glottolog’s family classification trees small arbitrary integer branch lengths (classification depth, time), minority real dated phylogenies branch lengths plausibly years (check dp_trees()’s source column, see functions’ documentation details) – distances different trees treated comparable; pair/society whose language different tree entirely distance . required cross_tree argument (default) controls second case: "na" records NA summarizing warning; planned "join_root" option (graft two trees root, using multiplier larger tree’s root--tip depth cross-tree distance) implemented yet – established method found (literature/web search turned nothing beyond supertree methods, require overlapping taxa don’t apply ), needs thought given units caveat , cross_tree = "join_root" currently errors explaining ; multiplier (default 2) reserved signature ships. get_society_data() searches assembles D-PLACE’s coded cultural data chosen set societies chosen set variables – named explicitly (var_id), found searching (category, type, search, passed straight dp_variables() combined ; least one four must supplied). format = "long" (default) returns one row per society/variable observation, like dp_variable_data(), variable metadata (var_name, var_category, var_type) added; format = "wide" returns one row per society one column per variable (named var_id), ready use directly analysis – "Continuous" columns numeric, "Categorical"/ "Ordinal" columns hold human-readable code label, society one recorded observation variable collapsed recent (year), warning. dp_variables()’s category argument now supports contains() partial/regex match, reason region needed : many category values several topics joined ", " (e.g. "Economy, Property, Subsistence"), exact match like category = "Subsistence" silently misses – category = contains("Subsistence") matches category string mentions term. supported type (fixed vocabulary). get_cult_distance() get_pairwise_cult_distance() gained variable-selection criteria get_society_data(): var_id now optional, category, type, /search can given instead (alongside ) select variable set searching – e.g. get_pairwise_cult_distance(soc_id, category = contains("Subsistence")) – combined passed straight dp_variables(), exactly get_society_data(). least one var_id/category/type/ search must supplied. Incidental fix: get_pairwise_cult_distance()’s “one variable requested” warning now based resolved variable set rather raw var_id argument, also fires variable(s) requested dropped unmatched, leaving one. dp_topics() splits every variable’s (often compound) category string individual topics returns one row per variable/topic pair (var_id, var_name, topic), browsing, counting, filtering single clean topic – e.g. sort(table(dp_topics()$topic), decreasing = TRUE) topic counts, dp_topics(topic = "Subsistence"). Topics split trimmed otherwise normalized: D-PLACE’s category text handful near-duplicate topics ("Labor"/"Labour", "Settlement"/"Settlements", "Dwelling"/"Dwellings", "Wealth Transactions"/"Wealth transactions", "War"/"Warfare"), spellings appear distinct topics rather silently merged – topic supports contains() (case-insensitive default) combine , e.g. topic = contains("Wealth"). dp_topic_list() returns sorted character vector every distinct topic – quick sort(unique(dp_topics()$topic)) see ’s available filtering . dp_topic_table() returns two-column tibble (topic, n_variables), one row per topic order dp_topic_list(), counting many variables carry – quick way see topics broad narrow filtering one. Bug fix: get_geo_distance() get_pairwise_geo_distance() longer fail whole call (“nodes connected graph.”) requested societies land route (e.g. ’re different continents, either island) – ‘geoGraph’‘s bundled world graphs sea-crossing edges removed, aren’t fully connected. Unreachable societies/pairs now dropped/recorded NA instead, warning, societies/pairs computable land-route distance returned. uses ’RBGL’ package (already dependency ‘geoGraph’ ), now listed Suggests. Performance: get_geo_distance() now uses geoGraph’s single-source dijkstraFrom() (one shortest-path tree point) instead dijkstraBetween()’s -pairs computation, also computing (discarding) every society--society distance. makes efficient large soc_id lists – previously cost grew roughly quadratically number societies requested, get_pairwise_geo_distance()’s inherently -pairs cost, even though get_geo_distance() ever needed point--society distances. Bug fix: get_geo_distance() get_pairwise_geo_distance() longer error “geoGraph’s … distance output expected structure” ordinary real-world input. Two distinct issues, reproducible live ‘geoGraph’ install (sandbox without ): dijkstraFrom()’s result named "<origin>:<destination>", just destination, get_geo_distance() didn’t account ; gPath2dist() returns dist object names() – rather named vector – whenever requested pairs span one distinct origin node (normal case 3+ societies), get_pairwise_geo_distance() didn’t account either (second issue predates dijkstraFrom() work latent since function first written). functions now verify structure underlying gPath object, reliably named either way. Breaking change: get_geo_distance() get_pairwise_geo_distance() gained required method argument (default) three genuinely different measures: "migration" (previous, behaviour – least-cost path across geoGraph’s world grid using bundled habitat-based edge costs, turns arbitrary graph-cost measure, physical distance despite past documentation implying otherwise – see ); "great_circle" (straight-line haversine distance km, ignoring land/sea entirely – needs neither ‘geoGraph’ graph, connectivity restrictions); "land_route_km" (real physical distance km along land-route "migration", weighting grid edge true great-circle length instead arbitrary cost, adding endpoint’s distance graph node snapped – without addition, routing two snapped nodes come shorter straight line original, un-snapped coordinates, breaking guarantee "land_route_km" always >= "great_circle" pair). output column now called geo_distance (distance_km) functions, since units depend method – named specifically (rather generic distance) can’t confused get_cult_distance()/get_pairwise_cult_distance()’s cult_distance column joined tibble (e.g. via [get_society_meta()]) plotted together. Existing code must updated pass method explicitly read geo_distance instead distance_km. Bug fix: values previously returned get_geo_distance() get_pairwise_geo_distance() (now method = "migration") mislabelled kilometres (distance_km) never physical distances – geoGraph’s bundled worldgraph.10k/worldgraph.40k objects ship habitat-based edge cost (land-land edges cost ~1) sea-crossing edges already removed, least-cost “distance” computed effectively hop count across graph’s grid, arbitrary units – confirmed geoGraph’s source vignette (labels exact quantity “arbitrary units”). Real physical distance now available via new method = "great_circle" "land_route_km" (see ); latter deliberately doesn’t use geoGraph’s setDistCosts(), since computes distance via fields::rdist.earth() without overriding function’s default miles, km – another silent-unit trap package now avoids entirely computing great-circle distance . dplace_societies gains xd_id column: D-PLACE’s cross-dataset identifier, linking societies different contributed datasets independently code real-world group – e.g. !Kung coded separately Binford’s dataset, Ethnographic Atlas, Standard Cross-Cultural Sample, three share xd_id = "xd1". column present D-PLACE’s CLDF data along previously dropped building package’s bundled data. societies (roughly 70% bundled snapshot) xd_id (NA) – haven’t cross-referenced another dataset. xd_id now also filter argument dp_societies() get_society(), full contains() support, e.g. get_society(xd_id = "xd1"). get_related_societies() finds every society sharing given society’s xd_id – e.g. get_related_societies("B72") returns !Kung codings Ethnographic Atlas SCCS alongside Binford’s . Accepts multiple society IDs (one row per queried/related pair result, input’s matches stay traceable); warns (doesn’t error) unknown society ID, society xd_id, xd_id currently society sharing – long least one requested society xd_id . dplace_societies gains lang_family_id/lang_family columns: society’s top-level Glottolog language family (e.g. lang_family_id = "indo1319", lang_family = "Indo-European"). Named lang_family* (plain family) avoid clashing D-PLACE’s “family” cultural/kinship variables, mean something unrelated. D-PLACE’s CLDF data family classification (leaf Glottocode per society), joined separate, pinned Glottolog CLDF release (see dplace_meta’s new glottolog_version/glottolog_source_repo columns, dp_citation(), now reports ) – every one 2837 distinct Glottocodes bundled D-PLACE snapshot matched. isolate (language known relatives, e.g. Zuni) top-level family, lang_family/lang_family_id equal language’s name/Glottocode case; NA small number societies glottocode . lang_family/lang_family_id now filter arguments dp_societies() get_society(), full contains() support – e.g. get_society(lang_family = "Indo-European") dp_societies(lang_family = contains("Austro")) match Austroasiatic Austronesian . dp_lang_family_list() returns sorted character vector every distinct top-level language family among coded (type = "society") societies – quick way see ’s available filtering lang_family. dp_lang_family_table() returns two-column tibble (lang_family, n_societies), one row per family order dp_lang_family_list(), counting many coded societies belong – quick way see families well represented filtering one.
